# Pitloom's catalogued messages: Embedded SBOMs

See also: `messages.md` (the index of every code), `../SKILL.md` (which holds
the rule: explain and relay, never run the fix).

### `datetime-not-recordable`

- **Level**: INFO.
- **Means**: The SBOM's creation time (--creation-datetime, else
  SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH) is before 1980, which a ZIP archive cannot record as a
  member's date (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 is the usual case).
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Dated the embedded SBOM's ZIP entry 1980-01-01; the SBOM's
  own created keeps the date given, so the wheel is still reproducible.
- **Nothing to do**: The line says why the entry's date and the SBOM's created
  differ; mention it only when the user asks about the dates.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  INFO: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM entry dated 1980-01-01, the earliest a ZIP archive can record; the SBOM's created keeps the true date [datetime-not-recordable]
  ```

### `sbom-name-conflict`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR (the Hatchling build hook only), the build fails
  and writes no wheel; no command stops on it.
- **Means**: The build hook's SBOM file name is also, ignoring letter case, the
  name of an SBOM Hatchling already places under .dist-info/sboms/ (an
  sbom-files entry, often a 'loom project' output of the same default name): one
  would overwrite the other, on a case-insensitive file system too.
- **SBOM effect**: not-written: no SBOM is written for the input.
- **Pitloom did**: Wrote nothing: the build hook fails the build.
- **Tell the user**: the two SBOM names collide, as the line says. They set
  [tool.pitloom] sbom-basename to another name, or drop the sbom-files entry,
  and build again. Do not edit the configuration for them; ask first, and with
  nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: FILE=<file>: also the name, ignoring case, of sbom-files entry '<path>'; set another sbom-basename in [tool.pitloom] or drop the entry [sbom-name-conflict]
  ```

### `wheel-sbom-ambiguous`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A wheel holds several SBOMs under its own .dist-info/sboms/ (PEP
  770 allows any number) and the command was not told which one to check.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Checked none of them: the wheel is reported failed and the
  command exits 1; the library (find_embedded_sbom) raises ValueError carrying
  the code.
- **The caller may fix**: The caller may run again with --sbom-filename naming
  one of the files the line lists, once for each SBOM to check.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>': <number> SBOMs under .dist-info/sboms/ (<members>); pass --sbom-filename [wheel-sbom-ambiguous]
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>': <number> SBOMs under .dist-info/sboms/ (<members>); pass sbom_filename [wheel-sbom-ambiguous]
  ```

### `wheel-sbom-conflict`

- **Level**: ERROR, WARNING. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and
  writes nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: An SBOM embedded in a wheel, or given to embed (embed-wheel
  --sbom), names a subject whose name or version differs from the wheel's own
  METADATA, compared as the ecosystem compares them (PEP 503 names, PEP 440
  versions): an SBOM of another package or release. One line per part that
  differs.
- **SBOM effect**: weaker: what the SBOM says is less sure.
- **Pitloom did**: As a WARNING (verify-wheel; embed-wheel with
  --allow-mismatch), went on: the status and exit status do not change. As an
  ERROR (verify-wheel --fail-on-mismatch: the wheel is reported failed and the
  command exits 1; embed-wheel --sbom: nothing is written, the command exits 1
  and the library raises ValueError carrying the code).
- **Tell the user**: the SBOM is not of this wheel, as the line says. They
  regenerate the SBOM for this wheel (or embed the right one) and run again; in
  CI, verify-wheel --fail-on-mismatch keeps a mismatch from passing. Do not pass
  --allow-mismatch or regenerate the SBOM for them; ask first, and with nobody
  to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM <part> <sbom-value> differs from the wheel's METADATA <wheel-value> [wheel-sbom-conflict]
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM <part> <sbom-value> differs from the wheel's METADATA <wheel-value> [wheel-sbom-conflict]
  ```

### `wheel-sbom-conflict/held`

- **Level**: WARNING, INFO.
- **Means**: An embed found another Pitloom SBOM already under the wheel's
  .dist-info/sboms/. One of type build or analyzed for the wheel's own name and
  version is the one the new embed supersedes; any other (a design or source
  SBOM, or one of another release) was shipped on purpose.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: The INFO line: removed the earlier SBOM from the rewritten
  wheel (and from RECORD). The WARNING: kept the other SBOM beside the new one;
  the wheel now holds both.
- **Tell the user**: Tell the user, after a WARNING only, that the wheel holds
  another SBOM, as the line says; if it is stale, they remove it and embed
  again. After the INFO line there is nothing to do. Do not remove an SBOM for
  them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': a Pitloom SBOM, not a build or analyzed one of this wheel's name and version; kept [wheel-sbom-conflict/held]
  INFO: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': an earlier Pitloom SBOM of this wheel; removed [wheel-sbom-conflict/held]
  ```

### `wheel-sbom-missing`

- **Level**: ERROR. As an ERROR, the command stops for that input and writes
  nothing for it (exit 1).
- **Means**: A wheel to verify or validate has no SBOM under its own
  .dist-info/sboms/ (PEP 770), or none of the file name given as
  --sbom-filename. Only a direct child of sboms/ is an embedded SBOM.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Reported the wheel as failed (STATUS=failed); a batch goes on
  with the next wheel and the command exits 1.
- **Tell the user**: the wheel carries no SBOM where PEP 770 puts it, as the
  line says. They embed one ('loom embed-wheel', 'loom wheel --embed', or the
  build hook) and check again, or give the right --sbom-filename. Do not embed
  for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>': no SBOM under .dist-info/sboms/ [wheel-sbom-missing]
  ERROR: ARCHIVE='<archive>': no SBOM under .dist-info/sboms/ named '<sbom-filename>' [wheel-sbom-missing]
  ```

### `wheel-sbom-unusable`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: A check of an embedded SBOM, or of one given to embed, could not be
  made: its format is not one Pitloom recognises (only SPDX 3 JSON-LD is; a
  CycloneDX file is not), so its extension is not checked or no validator runs;
  or its subject's name and version cannot be compared with the wheel's METADATA
  (PEP 503 names, PEP 440 versions): a side states none, a version is not a PEP
  440 version, or the SBOM has no SpdxDocument whose rootElement leads (through
  a software_Sbom) to a software_Package or ai_AIPackage. Only the first
  rootElement is followed.
- **SBOM effect**: weaker: what the SBOM says is less sure.
- **Pitloom did**: Skipped that check, never counting it as a mismatch:
  verify-wheel and embed-wheel go on, validate-wheel reports the wheel as
  skipped (STATUS=skipped), and no exit status changes.
- **Tell the user**: which check was not made and why, as the line says; the
  wheel and its SBOM may still disagree. If the SBOM is theirs, they regenerate
  it in SPDX 3 JSON-LD with the package as its subject. Do not edit the SBOM for
  them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': SBOM format not recognised; extension not checked [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': no validator for the SBOM's format; not validated [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM name and version not cross-checked: the wheel's METADATA states neither [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM <part> not cross-checked: the wheel's METADATA states none [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM <part> not cross-checked: the SBOM's subject states none [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM <part> not cross-checked: neither the wheel's METADATA nor the SBOM's subject states one [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM version not cross-checked: the wheel's METADATA version <wheel-value> is not a PEP 440 version [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM version not cross-checked: the SBOM's version <sbom-value> is not a PEP 440 version [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM name and version not cross-checked: the SBOM is not SPDX 3 JSON-LD [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM name and version not cross-checked: the SBOM has no SpdxDocument [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM name and version not cross-checked: the SpdxDocument has no usable rootElement [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM name and version not cross-checked: the software_Sbom has no usable rootElement [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>': SBOM name and version not cross-checked: the SBOM's subject is of type <sbom-value>, not a package [wheel-sbom-unusable]
  ```

### `wheel-sbom-wrong-format`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: An SBOM embedded in a wheel is in a format Pitloom recognises (SPDX
  3 JSON-LD) but its file name does not end in that format's recommended
  extension (.spdx3.json), which tools that look for an SBOM by name go by.
- **SBOM effect**: none: the SBOM states what the input holds.
- **Pitloom did**: Verified the rest; the wheel's status and the exit status do
  not change.
- **Tell the user**: the embedded SBOM's name lacks its recommended extension,
  as the line says. They embed it again under a name ending in that extension
  (embed-wheel --sbom-basename), if tools that read it need one. Do not re-embed
  for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: ARCHIVE='<archive>' ENTRY='<member>': SBOM does not end in <extension>, its format's recommended extension [wheel-sbom-wrong-format]
  ```

## Summaries

A summary is an `INFO:` line that reports what a run did under its own rule (a
count, the key it wrote), with no condition to name: it carries no code, and
there is nothing to do.

- loom validate-wheel found every wheel's embedded SBOM valid (schema and
  SHACL).

  ```text
  INFO: validate-wheel: <number> wheel(s) valid
  ```

- loom validate-wheel found no invalid SBOM, but could not validate some, their
  format having no validator (a wheel-sbom-unusable WARNING names each).

  ```text
  INFO: validate-wheel: <number> wheel(s) valid, <skipped> skipped (no validator for their format)
  ```

- loom verify-wheel found every wheel's SBOM where PEP 770 puts it; the WARNING
  lines before it, if any, say what else it found.

  ```text
  INFO: verify-wheel: <number> wheel(s) OK
  ```
